mainTopic: Why the תורה needs each פסוק about punishing killers: no double punishment, no ransom, the עגלה ערופה, death by סייף, and 'כל חרם'.
overview: This amud first finishes showing that a person who gets מיתה gets no second punishment. One פסוק covers death with money, and another covers death with lashes, and a צריכא shows that each is needed. Then the גמרא goes through a series of פסוקים about killers and asks of each one, 'why do I need it?' The two 'לא תקחו כופר' פסוקים teach that money cannot replace death for a מזיד or replace גלות for a שוגג. 'ולארץ לא יכופר' teaches that the עגלה ערופה does not free a killer who is found later. 'ואתה תבער הדם הנקי' compares killers to the calf, so סייף is done at the neck, but not with a cleaver, because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך', which means choosing a kind death. 'כל חרם' teaches either that a ערכין vow on a condemned man means nothing, or, for רבי חנניא בן עקביא, that a בית דין death penalty can never be bought off with money. The amud ends as רמי בר חמא begins to explain why 'כל חרם' is needed beside 'לא תקחו כופר'. His answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The second verse covers death and lashes
steps.stepSummary: This finishes the earlier answer. The second פסוק teaches that someone who gets מיתה does not also get מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one verse is about death and lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer it started just before. One פסוק was about death and money, and this second one is about death and lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that a person who is חייב מיתה gets only the biggest punishment. Two פסוקים teach this rule, and each one covers a different pair of punishments. This line names the second pair: מיתה and מלקות.

phrases.english: And one is about death and lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the two-part answer that began before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the verses: each verse covers a different pair of punishments.
steps.terutzMaskana: One verse is about death plus money, and the other is about death plus lashes.

steps.title: Why death and money alone would not teach death and lashes
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the צריכא: from 'death and money' alone, we would not know the rule for 'death and lashes'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the תורה had only taught death and money, I would say the reason is that we don't punish a person once in his body and once in his wallet. But death and lashes are both to his body, so I might say it is just a 'long death' and we should give both.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why we need both פסוקים. It starts by showing that the 'death and money' פסוק by itself would not be enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Death and money are two different kinds of punishment, one to the body and one to the wallet, and we don't combine kinds. Lashes and death are both to the body. So I might think lashes followed by death is really one long death, and that it should be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is necessary (both teachings are needed)

steps.confusionAlert: 'אֵימָא' means 'I might have said'. It is a mistaken idea that the גמרא is about to reject, not the actual הלכה.

phrases.english: And both are necessary, for if it had taught us only death and money,
I would say it is because one punishment is to his body
and one is to his money, and that we do not do.
But with death and lashes,
where both this and that are to his body,
I might say it is just a drawn-out death,
so let us do it to him.
phrases.notes: Give him the lashes and then the death penalty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Justifies why the second verse (step 1) is needed in addition to the first.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכא: a reason that applies only to one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Death plus lashes might be allowed because it is all one long bodily punishment.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate verse is needed for death and lashes.

steps.title: Why death and lashes alone would not teach death and money
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the צריכא: from 'death and lashes' alone, we would not know the rule for 'death and money'. So both פסוקים are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had only taught death and lashes, I would say the reason is that we don't give two punishments to the body. But with death and money, one is to the body and one is to the wallet, so I might say we give both. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now runs the argument the other way around. Then it concludes that both פסוקים are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason behind 'death and lashes' might only be that the body cannot take two punishments. That reason would not apply to money, because money is a different area. So each פסוק teaches something the other could not.
steps.whatToRemember: A person who gets מיתה never also gets מלקות or a money payment. Each of these is learned from its own פסוק, because neither case can be learned from the other.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only death and lashes,
I would say it is because two punishments to his body we do not do.
But death and money,
where one is to his body and one is to his money,
I might say: let us do both to him.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in step 2.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both verses are needed, because the reason for each case does not carry over to the other.

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about no ransom for a murderer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the פסוק 'ולא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח' comes to teach.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer.' Why do I need this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question. It quotes a פסוק about not taking money from a רוצח and asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know that a person who gets death does not also pay money. So it seems this פסוק has nothing left to teach, and the גמרא wants to know its purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: Ransom; a payment to buy one's way out

phrases.english: "And you shall take no ransom for the life of a murderer"
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא תִקְחוּ כוֹפֶר לְנֶפֶשׁ רוֹצֵחַ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since 'no money together with death' is already known, the גמרא asks what this verse adds.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the verse 'ולא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח' comes to teach.

steps.title: Money cannot replace the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that you may not take money from a רוצח in place of killing him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תורה is saying: Do not take money from him and let him off the death penalty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this פסוק teaches something new. The money is not taken in addition to death; it cannot be taken instead of death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier rule said we don't take money as an extra punishment on top of death. This פסוק says something different: money cannot buy a murderer out of his death penalty.

phrases.english: Because the Merciful One said:
Do not take money from him
and let him off from execution.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: לָא תִּשְׁקוֹל מָמוֹנָא מִינֵּיהּ וְתִפְטְרֵיהּ מִקְּטָלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse forbids taking money in place of the death penalty.

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about no ransom for one who fled?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about the next פסוק, the one about a killer who ran to an עיר מקלט.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'You shall take no ransom for him who fled to his city of refuge.' Why do I need this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same kind of question about the very next פסוק. This one is about an accidental killer who runs to an עיר מקלט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same question as before, now asked about the punishment of exile. The גמרא wants to know what this second כופר פסוק adds.

keyTerms.meaning: City of refuge, where an accidental killer goes

phrases.aramaic: ״לֹא תִקְחוּ כוֹפֶר לָנוּס אֶל עִיר מִקְלָטוֹ״
phrases.english: "You shall take no ransom for him who fled to his city of refuge"
why do I need it?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא תִקְחוּ כוֹפֶר לָנוּס אֶל עִיר מִקְלָטוֹ לְמָה לִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the companion verse the same question asked in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the verse about the city of refuge comes to teach.

steps.title: Money cannot replace exile
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that you may not take money from an accidental killer in place of sending him to גלות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תורה is saying: Do not take money from him and let him off from exile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this פסוק forbids paying money to get out of גלות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer has the same structure as step 5, but it is about exile instead of death. An accidental killer cannot pay his way out of going to the עיר מקלט.

keyTerms.meaning: Exile to a city of refuge

phrases.english: Because the Merciful One said:
Do not take money from him
and let him off from exile.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַחֲמָנָא: לָא תִּשְׁקוֹל מָמוֹנָא מִינֵּיהּ וְתִפְטְרֵיהּ מִן גָּלוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The verse forbids taking money in place of exile.

steps.title: Why two verses for the same idea?
steps.stepSummary: Both פסוקים teach 'no money in place of punishment'. So why do we need two?
steps.simpleTranslation: And why do I need two verses?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answers just given. Both פסוקים seem to say the same thing, so one should have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both steps 5 and 7 teach one principle: money cannot replace a punishment. If the principle is the same, it seems the תורה could have written it once.

phrases.english: And why do I need two verses?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for both verses explained in steps 5 and 7.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both verses teach the same principle, so one verse should be enough.

steps.title: One for an accidental killer, one for an intentional killer
steps.stepSummary: One פסוק is about a שוגג (accidental) and one is about a מזיד (intentional).
steps.simpleTranslation: One is about an accidental killer and one is about an intentional killer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each פסוק covers a different kind of killer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מזיד gets the death penalty, so the 'רוצח' פסוק is about him. The שוגג goes to גלות, so the 'עיר מקלט' פסוק is about him. The next steps explain why one could not be learned from the other.

phrases.english: One is about an unintentional killer and one is about an intentional one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzMaskana: Each verse applies to a different kind of killer.

steps.title: The intentional case alone would not teach the accidental case
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the צריכא: from a מזיד alone, we would not know that a שוגג also cannot pay.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If the תורה had only taught the intentional killer, I would say the reason is that his sin is severe. But an accidental killer's sin is not severe, so I might say he can pay.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that the פסוק about the מזיד would not be enough to teach the case of the שוגג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The intentional killer did a terrible sin, and that could be the reason he cannot pay. The accidental killer is much less guilty. So without a separate פסוק, I might let him pay instead of going to גלות.

keyTerms.meaning: I might say not (the rule would not apply)

phrases.english: And both are necessary, for if it had taught us only the intentional killer,
I would say it is because his sin is severe.
But an unintentional killer, whose sin is not severe —
I might say not.
phrases.notes: I might think the 'no ransom' rule doesn't apply here, so the accidental killer could pay instead of going into exile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the צריכא supporting the answer of step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The accidental killer, being less guilty, could pay instead of going into exile.
steps.terutzMaskana: A separate verse is needed for the שוגג.

steps.title: The accidental case alone would not teach the intentional case
steps.stepSummary: The second half of the צריכא: from a שוגג alone, we would not know that a מזיד also cannot pay. So both פסוקים are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had only taught the accidental killer, I would say the reason is that no life is lost. But with an intentional killer, a life is lost, so I might say he can pay. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא runs the argument the other way around. Then it concludes that both פסוקים are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The accidental killer only goes to גלות, so refusing his money costs him no life. The intentional killer will be killed, and to save a life I might allow money. So the תורה needed a separate פסוק to say no.
steps.whatToRemember: Money can never replace the punishment of a killer. An intentional killer cannot pay to escape death, and an accidental killer cannot pay to escape גלות. Each rule needs its own פסוק.

phrases.english: And if it had taught us only the unintentional killer,
I would say it is because there is no loss of life.
phrases.notes: The accidental killer is only sent to exile, not put to death.

phrases.english: But an intentional killer, where there is loss of life —
I might say not.
So both are necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכא begun in step 10.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both 'no ransom' verses are needed: one for the intentional killer (death) and one for the accidental killer (exile).

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about atoning for the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק 'ולארץ לא יכופר' is needed, since the rule that a killer must die and cannot pay is already taught.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And no atonement can be made for the land for the blood spilled in it, except by the blood of the one who spilled it.' Why do I need this verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finds another פסוק that also seems to say a killer must die and cannot pay instead. It asks what this extra פסוק is for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In steps 4-11 the גמרא showed that two פסוקים teach 'no money instead of punishment', one for a שוגג and one for a מזיד. This third פסוק also says only the killer's blood brings atonement, which looks like the same rule again. So it seems extra.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who spilled it (the killer)
Why do I need it? A question about an extra-looking source

phrases.english: "And no atonement can be made for the land for the blood
that was spilled in it
except by the blood of the one who spilled it"
why do I need it?
phrases.notes: He means: we already know a killer cannot pay money instead of dying, so what is this verse adding?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After proving both earlier פסוקים are needed, the גמרא checks a third פסוק that seems to repeat the same rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'ולארץ לא יכופר'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its message, that only the killer's death atones, already seems covered by the פסוקים forbidding money in place of punishment.

steps.title: The verse teaches that the calf does not free a killer found later
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for a ברייתא: if the עגלה ערופה was already done and then the killer is found, he is still punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that if the calf's neck was broken and afterward the killer was found, we do not let him go free? Because it says: 'And no atonement can be made for the land for the blood spilled in it...'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this פסוק has its own job. It teaches that the עגלה ערופה ceremony does not free the real killer if he is found afterward.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think the calf already brought atonement for this murder, so the killer is off the hook. The פסוק says atonement comes only through the killer's own blood, not through the calf. So this is a new rule, not a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: Like what was taught in a ברייתא
The calf whose neck is broken when a murder victim is found and the killer is unknown

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the עגלה ערופה only covers the community while the killer is unknown; it never replaces the killer's own punishment.

phrases.english: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know that if the calf's neck was broken
and afterward the killer was found,
from where do we know that we do not let him go free?
As it says: "And no atonement can be made for the land for the blood
that was spilled in it, etc."
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the end of the verse: only by the killer's blood, and not by the calf's.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 12 by giving the פסוק its own separate teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the verse to a different law (מיבעי ליה)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seemed to repeat that a killer cannot pay to avoid death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that the עגלה ערופה does not free a killer who is found later.

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about removing innocent blood?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק 'ואתה תבער הדם הנקי מקרבך' is needed, since it also seems to say a killer must be punished.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'And you shall remove the innocent blood from your midst.' Why do I need it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the last פסוק of the עגלה ערופה section. It also seems to say the killer must be punished, so the גמרא asks what it adds.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already know the killer must die and that the calf does not free him. This פסוק seems to say the same thing again, so the גמרא wants to know its own purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: You shall remove / get rid of
The innocent blood (the guilt of the murder)

phrases.english: "And you shall remove the innocent blood from your midst"
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of question as step 12, now about another פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'ואתה תבער הדם הנקי מקרבך'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: It seems to repeat what is already known: the killer must be punished.

steps.title: The verse teaches that death by sword is at the neck
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק links all killers to the עגלה ערופה: just as the calf is killed at the neck, so a killer put to death by סייף is killed at the neck.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: From where do we know that those put to death by the sword are killed at the neck? The verse says: 'And you shall remove the innocent blood from your midst.' All killers are compared to the עגלה ערופה. Just as there it is at the neck, so too killers are put to death at the neck.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that this פסוק teaches how death by סייף is done. Because the פסוק sits right next to the עגלה ערופה, killers are compared to the calf, which is killed at the neck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'innocent blood' close the עגלה ערופה section but talk about killers in general. That connects the two. So the calf's way of dying (at the neck) tells us where a killer's punishment of סייף is done.

keyTerms.meaning: Sword; one of the four death penalties of בית דין
They were compared (by placing them together in the verse)

phrases.english: It is needed for what was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know, for those put to death by the sword,
that it is done at the neck?
The verse teaches:
"And you shall remove the innocent blood from your midst"

phrases.aramaic: הוּקְשׁוּ כׇּל שׁוֹפְכֵי דָמִים לְעֶגְלָה עֲרוּפָה,
phrases.english: all killers are compared to the calf whose neck is broken.
Just as there, it is done at the neck,
so too killers are put to death at the neck.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 by giving the פסוק a new teaching about how סייף is done.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the verse to a different law through a comparison (היקש)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse seemed to just repeat that the killer must be punished.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse compares killers to the עגלה ערופה, teaching that סייף is at the neck.
steps.whatToRemember: Every 'extra' פסוק has its own job: one teaches the calf does not free the killer, and one teaches that סייף is at the neck.

steps.title: Should killers be killed exactly like the calf?
steps.stepSummary: If killers are compared to the עגלה ערופה, maybe they should also be killed with a cleaver from the back of the neck, like the calf.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as there it is done with a cleaver and from the back of the neck, here too should it be with a cleaver and from the back of the neck?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further. If we learn 'neck' from the calf, why not also learn the calf's other details: a cleaver, from behind?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries over all the details of the case. The calf is killed with a heavy cleaver from the back of the neck. So the גמרא asks why the killer should not be killed in exactly that way.

keyTerms.meaning: A cleaver, a heavy chopping knife
From the back of the neck

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה לְהַלָּן בְּקוֹפִיץ וּמִמּוּל עוֹרֶף,
phrases.english: If so, just as there it is with a cleaver and from the back of the neck,
here too should it be with a cleaver and from the back of the neck?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison from step 15 should go.
steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison of killers to the עגלה ערופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison teaches 'at the neck', it should also teach the calf's other details: a cleaver and from behind.

steps.title: Love your neighbor: choose a kind death for him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן in the name of רבה בר אבוה says the פסוק 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' teaches that we must choose a kind death for him, so the cleaver is not used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: The verse says, 'And you shall love your neighbor as yourself.' Choose for him a kind death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison only teaches 'at the neck', but not the cleaver or from behind. That is because another פסוק tells us to choose a kind death even for someone being put to death.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Chopping with a cleaver from behind is a harsh, ugly way to die. 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך' requires us to treat even a condemned man with care. So it limits the comparison, and the killer is killed at the neck by the sword, but in a kinder way.

keyTerms.meaning: Choose for him a kind (dignified) death

steps.whatToRemember: Killers put to death by סייף are killed at the neck (learned from the עגלה ערופה), but not with a cleaver from behind, because of מיתה יפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: The idea of מיתה יפה, from 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך', shapes how all of בית דין's death penalties are carried out.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ,
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
The verse says: "And you shall love your neighbor as yourself"
Choose for him a kind death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by limiting the comparison to the calf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Another פסוק limits how far the comparison goes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Killers should be killed just like the calf, with a cleaver from behind.
steps.terutzMaskana: Killers are killed at the neck, but in a kind way, because of 'ואהבת לרעך כמוך'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Death by סייף is at the neck, but we must choose a kind death, not the cleaver from behind.

steps.title: Why do we need the verse about 'כל חרם'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the פסוק 'כל חרם אשר יחרם מן האדם לא יפדה' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Any person who is condemned to death shall not be redeemed." Why do I need this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps up its pattern and asks about another פסוק that seems to say a condemned person cannot escape. Why would the תורה need it?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, the פסוק says a condemned person cannot be 'redeemed', so he cannot buy his way out of the death penalty. The גמרא assumes the תורה does not repeat itself, so this פסוק must teach something new.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set apart; here, a person condemned to death
Shall not be redeemed (cannot be bought free)

phrases.english: "Anything dedicated that is dedicated
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:29. Here the גמרא reads it as talking about a person condemned to death.

phrases.english: of men shall not be redeemed"
why do I need it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as Step 14: after one פסוק is explained, the גמרא asks why another פסוק on the same subject is needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the פסוק 'כל חרם אשר יחרם מן האדם לא יפדה'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The idea that a condemned person cannot escape death seems already known, so this פסוק looks extra.

steps.title: The verse teaches that a valuation vow on a condemned man means nothing
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק is needed for a ברייתא: if someone vows the ערך of a person already sentenced to death, his words mean nothing. This applies only after the verdict is final.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what a ברייתא teaches: Where do we learn that if a man is being taken out to be killed, and someone says 'I take upon myself to give his value', he has said nothing? As it says: 'Any person who is condemned shall not be redeemed.' You might think this is true even before his verdict was finished. So the פסוק says 'of men', meaning not a whole man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the פסוק teaches a new law about ערכין vows. A vow to give the value of a man already sentenced to death does not count.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once his verdict is final, the condemned man is treated as if already dead, so a vow on his 'value' has nothing to take hold of. The word 'מן האדם' ('part of a man') limits this. Before the verdict he is still a 'whole man', and the vow does count.

keyTerms.meaning: One being taken out to be executed
"His value is upon me": a vow to give the Temple the Torah's set amount for a person
He said nothing; the words have no legal effect

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that once the verdict is final, a condemned person loses his standing as a 'whole person' in certain laws.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which was taught in a ברייתא:
From where do we know, about one going out to be killed,
and someone said "His value is upon me,"
phrases.notes: This is a vow to give the Temple the fixed value the Torah sets for that person.

phrases.english: from where do we know that he said nothing?
As it says: "Anything dedicated that is dedicated
of men shall not be redeemed."

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל אַף קוֹדֶם שֶׁנִּגְמַר דִּינוֹ כֵּן?
phrases.english: You might think it is so even before his verdict was finished?
So the פסוק says: "of men"
and not the whole man.
phrases.notes: 'מן' means 'part of'. Only a man already sentenced counts as 'part of a man'; before the verdict he is still whole.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 18 by giving the פסוק a new job.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the פסוק to a different law (ערכין vows on a condemned man)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק only repeats that a killer cannot escape death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that a valuation vow on someone already sentenced to death has no effect, but before the verdict it does.

steps.title: What does רבי חנניא בן עקביא learn from the verse?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקביא holds that a condemned man can be valued because the amount is fixed. So for him the previous answer does not work. What does he learn from the פסוק?
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, who says a condemned man can be valued because his value is fixed, what does he do with this 'כל חרם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of Step 19 using a תנא who disagrees with that ברייתא. For him, the פסוק still seems to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ערכין amounts are set by the תורה by age and gender, not by what the person is worth. So רבי חנניא בן עקביא says even a condemned man, as long as he is alive, can be valued. He does not learn Step 19's law from the פסוק, so the original question returns for him.

keyTerms.meaning: He can be valued (a ערכין vow on him counts)
His value is fixed (set by the Torah)
What does he do with it? What does he learn from it?

phrases.english: And according to רבי חנניא בן עקביא, who said:
He can be valued, because his value is fixed,
this "כל חרם", what does he do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on Step 19 by pointing to a תנא who does not accept its law.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי חנניא בן עקביא lets a condemned man be valued, so he cannot use the פסוק to teach that the vow is void. The פסוק again has no clear job for him.

steps.title: No paying money to escape a בית דין death penalty
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנניא בן עקביא uses the פסוק for a ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל: unlike those liable to death בידי שמים, who can pay כופר, a person sentenced to death by בית דין cannot pay to escape.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs it for what a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: Since we find that people liable to death by Heaven can give money and get atonement, as it says 'If a ransom is placed on him', you might think the same is true for people liable to death by human courts. So the פסוק says: 'A person condemned by men shall not be redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי חנניא בן עקביא learns a different law from the פסוק. A person sentenced to death by בית דין can never pay money instead.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner of an ox that killed is liable to death בידי שמים, yet the Torah lets him pay כופר. One might compare a בית דין death penalty to that case. The פסוק 'לא יפדה' blocks the comparison: for death at the hands of men, no ransom works.

keyTerms.term: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to death by Heaven, not by בית דין
Ransom money paid instead of a punishment
By human hands, meaning by בית דין

steps.whatToRemember: Every תנא finds a job for 'כל חרם'. For the first ברייתא, it voids a ערכין vow on a condemned man. For רבי חנניא בן עקביא, it teaches that a בית דין death penalty can never be swapped for money, unlike death בידי שמים.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a basic rule: a death penalty given by בית דין cannot be bought off with money.

phrases.english: He needs it for that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: רבי ישמעאל, son of רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, says:
Since we found that those liable to death by Heaven
give money and receive atonement,
as it says: "If a ransom is placed upon him."
phrases.notes: שמות 21:30, about the owner of an ox that killed a person.

phrases.english: You might think it is so even for death by human hands?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חֵרֶם מִן הָאָדָם לֹא יִפָּדֶה״.
phrases.english: So the פסוק says: "One condemned by men shall not be redeemed."

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְתַנְיָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20 by giving the פסוק a different job that fits רבי חנניא בן עקביא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigns the פסוק to a different law for this תנא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since a person liable to death בידי שמים can pay כופר, a person liable to death by בית דין could pay too.
steps.terutzMaskana: A person sentenced to death by בית דין cannot be redeemed with money.

steps.title: The extra word 'all' includes the lighter death penalties
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל continues. The basic rule (no money in place of a בית דין death penalty) clearly covers the severe death penalties. The word 'כל' in 'כל חרם' adds the lighter ones too.
steps.simpleTranslation: So far I only know this about the severe death penalties, where there is no כפרה for doing the sin by accident. How do I know it also applies to the lighter death penalties, where there is a כפרה for doing it by accident? The פסוק says 'כל חרם' ('ALL that is devoted').
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from the last step keeps going. It uses the word 'כל' ('all') to stretch the rule to the lighter death penalties too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One might think only the most serious sins have no way out through money. But some sins that carry a death penalty do have a way to atone for the accidental version (a קרבן חטאת), so maybe their deliberate version could be bought off. The word 'כל' teaches that no case of מיתת בית דין can be traded for money.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Severe' death penalties: here, sins with no כפרה for the accidental version
'Lighter' death penalties: sins whose accidental version can be atoned for
Doing a sin by accident, without meaning to
Atonement, such as bringing a קרבן חטאת

steps.confusionAlert: 'Severe' and 'lighter' here are NOT about which method of execution is used. They depend on one question: did the Torah give a כפרה for doing the sin by accident? A sin like שבת can carry סקילה and still count as 'lighter' here.

phrases.english: And I have only the severe death penalties
whose accidental violation was not given atonement,
the lighter death penalties
whose accidental violation was given atonement, from where do we know?
phrases.notes: He means: from where do we know you can't pay money in place of execution for these too?

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "All that is devoted."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:29. The word 'כל', 'all', is what brings in the lighter cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל that was brought in Step 21 as רבי חנניא בן עקביא's use of the פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: No death penalty given by בית דין, whether severe or lighter, can be swapped for a money payment. The word 'כל' teaches this.

steps.title: Why is 'כל חרם' needed if 'לא תקחו כופר' already teaches this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. The פסוק 'לא תקחו כופר' already teaches that you may not take money from a condemned person and free him. So what does 'כל חרם' add?
steps.simpleTranslation: But don't you already learn from 'לא תקחו כופר' that you may not take money from him and let him go? Why do I need 'כל חרם'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the ברייתא it just quoted. It says another פסוק already teaches the same rule, so 'כל חרם' looks extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself without a reason. The פסוק about a murderer, 'לא תקחו כופר לנפש רוצח', already forbids taking money to free a condemned person. If so, using 'כל חרם' for the very same rule seems pointless.

keyTerms.meaning: A money payment given instead of a punishment
And free him (exempt him from the punishment)
Why do I need it? (the verse looks extra)

phrases.english: But don't you already, from "You shall take no ransom"
learn from it —
do not take money from him and free him?
Why do I need "All that is devoted"?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָא מִמֵּילָא מִ״לֹּא תִּקְחוּ כּוֹפֶר״ שָׁמְעַתְּ מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל (Steps 21-22) by saying its פסוק looks unnecessary.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of 'כל חרם' in the ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל to teach that a person sentenced by בית דין cannot pay to escape.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redundancy: 'לא תקחו כופר' already teaches that you may not take money and free a condemned person, so 'כל חרם' adds nothing.

steps.title: רמי בר חמא begins: the verse is needed
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא answers that 'כל חרם' is needed, because without it we might have reasoned wrongly. His full explanation continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: It is needed. You might have thought...
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא starts to defend the ברייתא. This line only sets up his answer, and the actual reasoning comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'סלקא דעתך אמינא' tells us he will show a mistaken idea we could have had if we only had 'לא תקחו כופר'. 'כל חרם' is needed to block that mistake. What the mistake is has not been said yet.

keyTerms.meaning: It might have entered your mind to say (a mistaken first thought is coming)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:
It is needed, for it might have entered your mind to say:
phrases.notes: The sentence breaks off here. What he thinks we might have said comes on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: אִיצְטְרִיךְ, סָלְקָא דַּעְתָּךְ אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to the challenge in Step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Necessity argument: shows that without the second פסוק we would have made a mistaken inference.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Introduced here but not yet spelled out: a mistaken conclusion one could draw from 'לא תקחו כופר' alone.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל חרם' is not extra. It is needed to block that mistaken conclusion (details continue on the next amud).
